evidence.detail: rs/d/m opens the exact configs/hovers.yaml file beneath the client cache/config root, parses it with SnakeYAML as a Map<Integer,String>, and copies the entries into an item-id keyed Trove map.
Its lookup method accepts an existing item-hover string plus item id and appends the configured description when present; the Client item-hover rendering path calls this method directly.
The runtime reload command emits the surviving message '<img=2> Item hover descriptions reloaded!', while the item-definition update path can insert per-item description overrides into the same map.

candidates.note: ItemHoverDescriptionConfig is the conservative semantic name for this exact hovers.yaml item-description table; it does not claim a verbatim original developer identifier.

evidence.detail: rs/d/p opens the exact configs/rarities.yaml file, parses item-id keys and rarity strings with SnakeYAML, and stores the resolved rarity enum in an item-id keyed Trove map.
The loader recognizes exactly uncommon, rare and legendary values and maps them to the three rs/d/p$a enum constants.
R28 ItemDefinition checks this map by item id and, when a mapped item name still carries the default @gre@ prefix, replaces that prefix with the selected rarity enum's display-format tag.

candidates.note: ItemRarityConfig is the conservative semantic name for this exact rarities.yaml item-id-to-rarity table; it does not claim a verbatim original developer identifier.

evidence.detail: rs/d/p$a is an enum with surviving exact constants UNCOMMON, RARE and LEGENDARY.
Each enum value owns the exact item-name formatting tag used by ItemDefinition: <col=65BFFF>, <col=BD73FF><shad=773494>, or <col=FFC81A><shad=9A7705>.
ItemRarityConfig maps rarities.yaml values to these enum constants, and ItemDefinition consumes the enum's formatting string for rarity-colored item names.

candidates.note: ItemRarity is the conservative semantic name for this exact three-tier item rarity enum; it does not claim a verbatim original developer identifier.
